Declare a validation rule

Source: R/rules.R
rule.Rd

Builds a rule for validate_rules(): a predicate over one column, or over the whole data frame, with a severity and a message. Use rules for the checks that are particular to a data set and that a schema cannot express: an age must be non-negative, an identifier must be unique, a release date must not precede an admission date. Rules live alongside a schema in a provenance record, which keeps the project-specific checks in data rather than scattered through code.

Usage

rule(
  name,
  expr,
  column = NULL,
  severity = c("warning", "fatal"),
  message = NULL
)

Arguments

name

Short identifier for the rule, a string; it names the issue in the result of validate_rules(), so give each rule a different name.

expr

A function, as described above.

column

Name of the column the rule applies to, or NULL (the default) for a table-level rule.

severity

"warning" (default) or "fatal". A fatal failure stops apply_schema_validation().

message

Human-readable description of what a failure means, a string. Defaults to "Rule '<name>' failed".

Value

A list of class c("bricklayer_rule", "list") with name, expr, column (NULL for a table rule), severity and message; it prints as one line.

Details

expr is a function. Given column, it receives that column and must return a logical vector the same length (TRUE = the row passes) or a single logical for a whole-column property. Given no column, it receives the whole data frame and must return a single logical. How the result is read is described in validate_rules().

Only the first element of name, column and message is kept. The rule is not run here. Errors: an empty or NA name; expr not a function; an empty or NA column; a severity other than "warning" or "fatal".

See also

validate_rules(), validate_schema() for the structural checks that need no rules.

Examples

# A column predicate, applied row-wise.
rule("age_non_negative", function(v) v >= 0, column = "age")
#> <rule> age_non_negative [warning] on `age`

# A whole-column property.
rule("id_unique", function(v) !anyDuplicated(v), column = "id",
     severity = "fatal")
#> <rule> id_unique [fatal] on `id`

# A table-level rule spanning two columns.
rule("dates_ordered", function(df) all(df$start <= df$end))
#> <rule> dates_ordered [warning] table-level

# with a message that says what a failure means
r <- rule("release_after_admission",
          function(d) all(d$release >= d$admission, na.rm = TRUE),
          message = "a release date precedes its admission date")
r$message
#> [1] "a release date precedes its admission date"

# the predicate must be a function, not an expression
try(rule("age_non_negative", "age >= 0", column = "age"))
#> Error : `expr` must be a function
